NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 9 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 8 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 3, 12:36 PM ET

Brock Purdy is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 9 DraftKings main slate at 21.1 DraftKings points for $6,800, against Las Vegas. Drake Maye (20.5, $7,000) and Patrick Mahomes (20.2, $6,100) are next.

Daniel Jones returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.66 projected points per $1,000 at $4,700.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 3, 12:36 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 9

Brock Purdy, SF vs LV ($6,800)

Brock Purdy carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 21.1 DraftKings points at $6,800, the 4th-highest on the entire main slate. That is 0.6 points clear of Drake Maye. The model includes 4.0 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.10 projected points per $1,000, 12th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Purdy averaged 21.1 points with a simulated floor of 8.5 and a ceiling of 38.5, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 10-point favorite at home against Las Vegas, with an implied team total of 30.75 in a game totaled at 51.5.

Drake Maye, NE vs GB ($7,000)

Drake Maye projects 2nd at the position with 20.5 DraftKings points at $7,000. The model includes 5.2 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 2.93 projected points per $1,000, 18th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Maye averaged 20.5 points with a simulated floor of 7.5 and a ceiling of 37.3, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. New England is a 2.5-point favorite at home against Green Bay, with an implied team total of 24.5 in a game totaled at 46.5.

Value: Daniel Jones, IND vs DAL ($4,700)

Daniel Jones projects for 17.2 DraftKings points at $4,700, which works out to 3.66 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 21 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. Across 10,000 simulations Jones averaged 17.2 points with a simulated floor of 6.7 and a ceiling of 31.4, and he holds 5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Indianapolis is a 6-point underdog at home against Dallas, with an implied team total of 22.75 in a game totaled at 51.5.
